Andrews received a genetically modified pig kidney in January last year, and then lived with it for nine months. He then received a human donor kidney, providing early proof that pig kidneys, while not yet a permanent solution, offer a bridge to transplants with human organs.

articles.headline: Running LLMs in the Browser with Three.js
articles.blurb: Three-LLM runs GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen, and Phi models locally in the browser by turning their inference graphs into Three.js TSL compute shaders on WebGPU. The project was created to see how far the general computer capabilities of Three.js and WebGPU can be pushed, and to see what today's small language models can do when they run in a browser. Three.js is known as a rendering library, but its WebGPU renderer also exposes storage buffers, compute dispatches, workgroup memory, atomics, and GPU readback. Large language models put all of those capabilities to work as they need hundreds of ordered compute dispatches, large matrix-vector products, reductions, persistent attention or recurrent state, and a tight loop between the GPU and JavaScript as each new token appears.

articles.headline: Win Report: How supply-side CRO lifted sign-ups by 15%
articles.blurb: Supply-side CRO can unlock major marketplace growth by optimizing for the actual intent of people who provide capacity, not just the customers who buy. A tutoring marketplace found that many tutor recruitment visitors came from job search sites, so it replaced a generic registration form with a real student job request, clear job details, pay information, and “apply” language. The change increased tutor applications by 15%, or about 20,000 additional tutors in the first year. Supply-side improvements may not show immediate revenue, but they can strengthen marketplace capacity and create an overlooked source of high-impact conversion gains.

articles.headline: The Impact of Content Freshness on AI Citations
articles.blurb: Content cited by AI assistants runs 25.7% fresher than what ranks organically on Google, with roughly half of all citations tracing to material updated in the last 13 weeks. That edge decays fast, with a median citation half-life of about 4.5 weeks across platforms. Retrieval systems re-rank the entire candidate pool on every query rather than relying on a persistent ranking, so recency becomes an early filter for weeding out sources that might already be wrong. Perplexity and Grok weigh it most heavily, while Google's AI Overviews stay tied to core search and actually skew slightly older.
